messages:
sre-bot: INCIDENT: Canary SLO burn detected for rollout r-2026-11-02 (canary group A). SLO: p95 latency > 800ms for 3m. Paging oncall.

sam: got the page, looking now. where's the error-rate dashboard? I only see request latency and infra metrics.

anya: same — traces are coming in for prod general but the canary tag doesn't exist on the trace view. dashboard filter for 'route:canary' returns empty.

mike: @sam @anya I'm on logs. seeing repeated 504s from the inference gateway during canary window. timestamps match the latency bump, but no error metric incrementing on redwood-api/error-rate.

sam: that's the problem — our synthetic that increments error-rate doesn't have the canary header. I think SPM config didn't pick up the new header. ops-runner, did the rollout include telemetry propagation?

ops-runner: confirmed rollout manifest had header-prop off for canary to avoid noisy downstream. that was intentional for perf test, but ops forgot to re-enable error tagging for this model.

anya: ahhh. so alerts are firing based on latency alone and we've lost our primary error signal. noisy pages expected.

mike: we should pause the canary and abort the rollout. canary is still at 10% traffic. no customer-facing spike in errors reported so far but latency SLO breach looks real.

sam: agree. executing abort now. command: ```redwoodctl rollout abort --id r-2026-11-02 --scope canary```

sre-bot: Deploy bot: Rollout r-2026-11-02 canary abort initiated by sam. Reason: telemetry mismatch and p95 latency SLO breach.

ops-runner: aborted successfully. verified traffic reverted to baseline.

lina: doing a quick sanity check on downstream model pool health — no OOMs, queue depth spiked briefly then drained. looks like KV cache misses causing high compute per-request.

anya: we need a mitigation and a blameless postmortem. immediate mitigation: re-enable canary telemetry header and re-run with a 1% canary and extended guardrails (longer ramp, higher sampling). also add a fallback rule: if error-rate metric missing, don't page on p95 alone for 5m.

sam: for oncall handoff: I'm in meeting in 20. @lina can you take the remainder of the monitoring/inspection and be primary for follow-ups? I'll paste current findings into the incident doc.

lina: yes taking handoff. i'll update the incident doc and tag @eng-runtime + @eng-ml.

mike: customer impact note — no support tickets yet, but we should mark as 'potentially affected' and keep an eye for errors in the next 2h. also recommend we mute the noisy latency-only alerts until telemetry is fixed.

ops-runner: added a temporary suppression rule: alert-routing -> latency-canary -> suppress for 30m with annotation "suppress until telemetry header re-enabled".

anya: adding follow-ups: (1) restore header propagation in canary manifests (2) add unit test to ensure telemetry header is present in manifest diffs (3) update alert runbook to include fallback when error-rate is unavailable.

sam: filing postmortem checklist now. handoff to @lina for next 24h monitoring. thanks all. :thumbsup:

lina: will monitor. leaving trace links and log snippets in the incident doc. final note: we should add a dashboard tile that explicitly shows telemetry-propagation flag per rollout so this doesn't blindside oncall next time.

sre-bot: Incident resolved (canary aborted). Summary: telemetry propagation disabled during canary caused missing error-rate signal; latency-based alerts paged oncall. Mitigation: abort, re-enable telemetry, suppress noisy alerts, add runbook updates.

sam: closing thread and moving to postmortem queue.
